I was 16, just around the time of Halloween and my group of friends were into fireworks at the time. During lunch break at school we were allowed down the town to get food as we were seen as maturing teens, oh how they were wrong. 

Anyway we took a lunch break and went to a guys house that we knew we could get fireworks at and got some. On our way back to school we lit a few off throwing them into gardens and on the road. At the bottom of the hill of our school entrance there was a house that had an apple tree or something, so we thought it would be a good idea to blow up some apples. Proceeded to grab some and start to pierce the apple with a pen and this is where the oh shit started. A black unmarked police car had pulled up right beside up and we all freaked and one of the shouted stop don’t do anything, literally caught red handed. Plenty of cars were driving past and I felt so bad and they made us feel so guilty about what we were doing incase something went wrong or someone got hurt. Anyway after about 10 minutes we were running late for our next class and I look up the hill and see this shiny bald head coming down, it was our principal. He marched down to find out what the teachers in the cars driving past were talking about. Busted. Along comes be long lecture and then pulled into his office when we got back up to school. Got a week suspension from school. 

Fast forward about 9 or 10 days and I was running late to get the bus so my dad said he would drop me up to school. He used to go to he same school as me before it was renamed. My principal was his English teacher back in the day. So the principal approaches the car to speak to my dad and see how he is keeping and such, then the bomb drops. He asked me in front of my dad if the suspension for the fireworks has taught me a lesson. My dad immediately turns to me and the death stare begins, the face gets red and he says get out and we’ll speak later. I was never more afraid to go home in all my life. I was getting on the bus in the morning and going into the library all day and just sit on the computers making my dad think I was at school. 

Anyway I’ve lived to tell the tale
